title: Exploring with my five senses
keyIdea: You have five senses. Eyes see, ears hear, your nose smells, your mouth tastes and your hands feel. Use them to find out about things. Only taste food that a grown-up gives you.

kid: You have five helpers on your body. Eyes see. Ears hear. Your nose smells. Your mouth tastes. Your hands feel.
Shut your eyes. Can you still find out? Yes! Your hands can feel a soft teddy. Your ears can hear a bell.
Say what you find. A drum is loud. A lamb is soft. A sock can be smelly. A pine cone is bumpy.
Look at a thing, feel it and sniff it. But do not taste it. Only taste food from a grown-up.
adult: Young children learn about the world through their senses. At two and three, the goal is to use looking, listening, touching, smelling and, when safe, tasting to explore everyday things, and to name the body part behind each sense: eyes, ears, nose, mouth (tongue) and hands (skin).

The lab gives each idea its own action. Children send a rainbow, bell, flower, strawberry and teddy to the body part that senses them, find toys in a feely bag by touch alone, choose sense words such as loud, sour, soft and smelly, sort food from things that are only for looking, and explore a pine cone with three senses while the mouth stays shut.

Common mistakes: mixing up which part does what (smelling with the mouth, hearing with the eyes); thinking you can only find out by looking; using a word from the wrong sense, such as calling a drum fluffy; and putting non-food things in the mouth. Touch is felt by skin all over the body; hands are just the part children use most.
Keep the safety rule simple and firm: we taste only food a grown-up gives us. Berries, mushrooms and plants outside, soap, pills and small objects are for looking, not tasting.

familyTip: On a walk, collect one safe natural thing, such as a pine cone, leaf or stone. Ask, "What can your eyes tell you? Your hands? Your nose?" Give one new word each time: bumpy, smooth, crunchy, smelly.

practice.prompt: Which part of you hears a bell ring?
practice.hint: A bell makes a sound. Which part takes in sounds?
practice.explain: Ears hear sounds, so your ears hear the bell. Eyes see it, but they can not hear it.

practice.prompt: You see {n} red balloons. Which part saw them?
practice.hint: Seeing colours is a job for one part. Which one?
practice.explain: Eyes see colours, so your eyes saw the {n} red balloons.

practice.prompt: A teddy is in a bag. You can not see it. How can you find out it is soft?
practice.hint: Which part can tell soft from hard?
practice.explain: Your hand can feel that it is soft, even with no looking. Never taste toys.

practice.prompt: Gran gives you {n} grapes for snack. Is it OK to taste them?
choices: Only if they are on the floor
practice.hint: Who gave you the grapes, and are grapes food?
practice.explain: Food a grown-up gives you is safe to taste, so you can eat the {n} grapes.

pool.hint: Sniff! Which part do you sniff with?
pool.explain: Your nose smells. Your mouth tastes and your ears hear.

pool.prompt: Which word tells how a drum sounds?
pool.hint: A drum is heard. Pick a word for ears.
pool.explain: Loud is a word for sounds. Fluffy is a feel word and sour is a taste word.

pool.prompt: You find a mushroom in the park. What do you do?
choices: Put it in your pocket to eat later
pool.hint: Is a park mushroom food from a grown-up?
pool.explain: Mushrooms outside can make you very ill. Look, but never taste.

pool.hint: Which word is a taste word?
pool.explain: Sour is a taste word, and a lemon is sour. Loud is for ears and bumpy is for hands.

pool.prompt: You hear {n} claps. Which part heard them?
pool.hint: Claps are sounds. Which part hears?
pool.explain: Ears hear sounds, so your ears heard the {n} claps.

pool.prompt: Which part tells you a pine cone is prickly?
pool.hint: Prickly is a feel word. Which part feels?
pool.explain: Your hands feel that the pine cone is prickly. Your nose smells it and your ears hear it.

pool.prompt: There are {n} cakes. Which part tastes them?
pool.hint: Which part do you eat with?
pool.explain: Your mouth and tongue taste, so your mouth tastes the {n} cakes.

pool.hint: What do you do with soap at the sink?
pool.explain: Soap is for washing. It may smell nice, but it is not food, so do not taste it.

visual.caption: Which sense does each word belong to? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: match things to body parts, find toys by touch, pick sense words, sort food from look-only things and explore a pine cone.
